record.paper_title: The average size of a connected vertex set of a graph-Explicit formulas and open problems
record.context_brief: High density with minimum degree at least three
record.original_question: Do there exist connected finite graphs whose minimum degree is at least 3 and whose connected-set density D(G)=A(G)/|V(G)| is arbitrarily close to 1? Equivalently, determine whether the supremum of connected-set density over minimum-degree-at-least-3 graphs is 1, and if not, how far above the known necklace-family density 5/6 it can be pushed.

evidence.quote: Question 8. Do there exist graphs with minimum degree at least 3 and density arbitrarily close to 1?
The necklaces Qn have a reasonable number of large separating sets, and the density is 5/6. By how much can this be increased?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite connected graph $G=(V,E)$, let $\mathcal{C}(G)$ denote the family of nonempty subsets $S\subseteq V$ such that the induced subgraph $G[S]$ is connected. Define the average size of a connected vertex set by
$$A(G)=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{C}(G)|}\sum_{S\in\mathcal{C}(G)}|S|,$$
and the connected-set density by $D(G)=A(G)/|V(G)|\in(0,1]$.

Question: Does there exist a sequence $(G_n)$ of finite connected graphs, each having minimum degree at least $3$, such that $D(G_n)\to 1$? Equivalently, is
$$\sup\{D(G):G\text{ finite connected, }\delta(G)\ge 3\}=1?$$
If the supremum is strictly less than $1$, determine how large it can be (in particular, exhibit graphs of minimum degree at least $3$ with density strictly greater than $5/6$, the density attained by the family of "necklace" graphs).
artifact.status_search_result: Haslegrave (J. Graph Theory, 2022; arXiv:2105.13332) proved that the connected-set density is bounded away from 1 for graphs with no vertex of degree 2, in particular for graphs with minimum degree at least 3. Moreover, any sequence of graphs whose minimum degree tends to infinity has density tending to 1/2. This answers the question negatively: the supremum is strictly less than 1.

status_evidence.title: The number and average size of connected sets in graphs with degree constraints
status_evidence.snippet: Any sequence of graphs with minimum degree tending to infinity must have connected set density tending to 1/2; density is bounded away from 1 for graphs with no vertex of degree 2.
status_evidence.claim: Density of min-degree ≥3 graphs is bounded away from 1, resolving the question negatively.

status_evidence.title: The number and average size of connected sets in graphs with degree constraints — Haslegrave, J. Graph Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Journal version of the same result on degree-constrained connected-set density.
status_evidence.claim: Published resolution showing supremum of density over min-degree-3 graphs is < 1.
